The page names the cave, not a territory; the Yogyakarta core is the reading.

wars.name: Java War

zones.text: the 'killing area' between the Progo and Bogowonto rivers, where the rebels were confined in 1828-1829 (disc read from the two river names)

wars.outcome: Dutch victory: the benteng system confined the rebels (258 forts, 133 built 1828-1829); Kyai Maja surrendered in November 1828, Diponegoro's remnants were defeated at Siluk on 17 September 1829, Sentot surrendered in October 1829 and Diponegoro was arrested on 28 March 1830. About 15,000 soldiers, up to 20,000 rebels and at least 200,000 civilians died. The Dutch annexed the princely states' outlying lands (mancanagara) and deposed Pakubuwono VI.
wars.note: The page also dates a rebel defeat near Gawok on 15 October 1826.

certainty.note: A guerrilla war: the page names fighting places and a 'killing area' between two rivers, not a front line.
